title: Ultrasonography in disaster medicine: a narrative review.
abstract: This narrative review aimed to critically appraise the diagnostic accuracy, clinical impact, and operational feasibility of ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) across the four domains of disaster medicine. A literature search was conducted following the SANRA and PRISMA-trAIce guidelines. Records were identified through an AI-assisted literature-discovery tool (the Undermind Deep-Search platform, interrogating the Semantic Scholar corpus) run on 15 June 2025, rather than through an independent structured multi-database search. Candidate references were screened manually against pre-specified eligibility criteria by a single reviewer, with the search parameters independently verified by the senior author. Of 71 records identified, 63 met the inclusion criteria. The included studies comprised 32 original studies, 10 systematic or scoping reviews, 20 narrative or operational papers, and one guideline. In CBRN scenarios, lung ultrasound demonstrated sensitivities of 90-97% for COVID-19 pneumonia versus 60-69% for chest radiography while minimizing healthcare worker exposure. For blast and ballistic injuries, FAST showed a pooled sensitivity of 92.1% (95% CI: 87.8-95.6) and specificity of 98.7% (95% CI: 96.0-99.9) for intra-abdominal hemorrhage. In natural disasters, ultrasound altered management in up to 44% of patients. Post-disaster applications included vascular access, tube confirmation, and complication monitoring. Ultraportable POCUS demonstrates diagnostic utility and operational feasibility across multiple disaster domains. However, evidence quality varies significantly, and standardized protocols remain lacking. Prospective studies linking ultrasound deployment to improved patient outcomes are needed. KEY POINTS: Question When disasters disable conventional imaging, how does ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography perform for diagnosis, triage, and procedural guidance across the four domains of disaster medicine? Findings Across 63 studies, FAST reached 92.1% pooled sensitivity for hemoperitoneum, lung ultrasound 90-97% versus 60-69% for radiography; management changed in up to 44%. Critical relevance statement This review critically appraises ultraportable ultrasound across all four disaster domains, showing that radiation-free bedside imaging accelerates triage, conserves scarce CT capacity, and extends radiological expertise through tele-guidance, while exposing an evidence base still lacking prospective outcome data.

title: MRI for restaging pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is a tumor with a dismal prognosis, as the majority of patients are diagnosed when the tumor is not resectable. Neoadjuvant treatment has significantly improved prognosis, but assessing treatment response can be challenging for radiologists. Given the fibrotic nature of the primary tumor, differentiating between residual viable tumor and fibrotic response can be difficult. MRI can have a role in reassessing the primary tumor and disease spread. In this review, we discuss MR techniques that can be used for this assessment, including routinely used sequences (e.g., DWI) and sequences that are not yet routinely included in pancreatic protocols (e.g., T1 mapping, ECV imaging, and USPIO contrast for nodal staging). KEY POINTS: Question Imaging assessment of the response of pancreatic adenocarcinoma to neoadjuvant treatment is difficult and still has limited accuracy. Findings Different MRI sequences and techniques have been suggested as possibly improving this assessment, reflecting on better patient management. Critical relevance statement We summarize the available evidence on MRI for restaging pancreatic carcinoma after neoadjuvant treatment.

title: Automated thigh muscle segmentation using foundation models: validation and impact of segmentation quality.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to validate a segmentation pipeline for the extraction of volumetric thigh muscle data, investigate the influence of demographics on segmentation performance, and investigate the influence of low-quality segmentations on quantitative performance and downstream metrics. Materials and methods Manual thigh muscle segmentations on axial T1-weighted spin echo thigh images of 364 (106 training and validation; 258 testing) participants of the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) were used. A trained YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection model generated labels and box predictions, that were passed to a fine-tuned foundation model (Segment Anything, Meta), which generated muscle segmentations. The quality of segmentations was assessed by two radiologists (none, minor, major issue), and Dice scores and mean bias versus manual segmentations were calculated in the testing dataset. Linear regression was used to calculate the associations of age, sex, and BMI with Dice scores. Results Dice scores ranged between 0.97 (quadriceps) and 0.89 (adductors). Exclusion of erroneous segmentations decreased mean bias by 0.06 mL across muscle groups; mean Dice of segmentations with versus without major issues was 0.90 versus 0.94. Female sex was associated with marginally lower Dice scores (beta -0.01, 95% CI: -0.02, -0.01, p < 0.001), while no other demographic feature showed significant associations. Conclusion Foundation models can be fine-tuned on a modest task-specific dataset to achieve segmentation accuracy comparable to bespoke networks, without training a dedicated architecture from scratch. Visually erroneous segmentations introduce only negligible degradation of quantitative performance and downstream metrics and may thus be challenging to identify by data-driven detection strategies. Key points Question Foundation models can be efficiently leveraged for robust segmentation on complex thigh muscle anatomy Findings Radiologist-identified erroneous segmentations introduced only negligible degradation of summary quantitative performance and are thus difficult to identify using statistical methods. Relevance statement Human-in-the-loop quality assurance post-validation adds limited value to improve downstream volumetric muscle metrics in foundation-model-based thigh segmentation. These findings carry implications for both research and potential clinical applications of muscle volume quantification, e.g., personalized therapeutic regimens.

title: Toward Clinically Actionable Prediction of Recurrence and Metastatic Progression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Purpose Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has high rates of early recurrence (ER), occult metastasis, and poor survival despite curative-intent therapy. Predictive factors and models span clinical, biomarker, imaging, radiomics, pathologic, and molecular domains, but clinical readiness remains uncertain. Methods We performed a systematic review in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses. Five databases were searched for studies evaluating predictors or models of PDAC recurrence, metastasis, lymph node metastasis (LNM), occult metastatic disease, disease-free survival (DFS) or recurrence-free survival, or recurrence patterns. Studies were screened and coded for end point, modality, model type, validation, discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and predictor timing. Results Of 234 full-text records, 208 studies were included, comprising 144 prediction models and 64 predictor/prognostic factor studies. Computed tomography/radiomics (141/208), clinical/electronic health record variables (104/208), and serum/urine biomarkers (46/208) were the most common modalities. External validation, calibration, and decision-curve analyses were reported in 52, 36, and 38 model studies, respectively. AUCs ranged from 0.70 to 0.92 for ER, 0.75-0.95 for LNM, and 0.71-0.88 for liver or occult metastasis; DFS/relapse-free survival models had C-indices of 0.62-0.82. One externally validated occult-metastasis model had a C-statistic of 0.56. Model maturity was limited by retrospective design, heterogeneous end points, incomplete calibration reporting, and postoperative variables in preoperative models. Conclusion Prediction models for PDAC recurrence and metastatic progression are rapidly expanding, particularly through radiomics, machine learning, and multimodal modeling. Clinical translation requires decision-aligned design, transparent reporting, external validation, calibration, interpretability, and prospective evaluation of clinical utility.

title: Coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodule presented as adrenal incidentaloma.
abstract: Adrenal hemangiomas are rare benign vascular tumors, an uncommon cause of adrenal incidentalomas. We report a patient with coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodules within the same adrenal gland. A 67-year-old man was referred for an incidental left adrenal mass. Noncontrast computed tomography revealed a 1.6 × 1.4 cm lesion with an unenhanced attenuation value of 40 Hounsfield units. Initial hormonal evaluation was unremarkable except for an elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR) of 115.6. On follow-up evaluation, the ARR decreased to 52.8, with a relatively low aldosterone concentration of 9.5 ng/dL (264 pmol/L; reference range, 2.52-39.2 ng/dL [69-1087 pmol/L]), yielding equivocal findings for primary aldosteronism. Serial imaging revealed growth to 3.4 × 2.8 cm over 3 years. title: Long-term cyclic ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone syndrome with extreme fluctuations and adrenal insufficiency.
abstract: A 77-year-old woman presented with worsening glycemic control and hypokalemia and was found to have adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent hypercortisolism with loss of diurnal cortisol variation and failure of suppression on low- and high-dose dexamethasone suppression tests. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral adrenal enlargement, whereas pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and chest CT failed to identify a source of ACTH secretion, leading to a diagnosis of occult ectopic ACTH syndrome. During 15 years of follow-up, she exhibited cyclic fluctuations in ACTH and cortisol concentrations, including episodes of severe hypercortisolism with ACTH levels exceeding 2000 pg/mL (>440 pmol/L) (reference range, 7.2-63.6 pg/mL [1.6-14.0 pmol/L]) and cortisol concentrations of 30-60 μg/dL (828-1656 nmol/L) (reference range, 6.2-19.4 μg/dL [171-535 nmol/L]), alternating with spontaneous remission. Serial imaging revealed dynamic adrenal morphological changes, with enlargement during hypercortisolemic phases and regression during remission. During treatment with ketoconazole, mitotane, and osilodrostat, the patient experienced recurrent significant hypocortisolic episodes, some of which were likely treatment-associated and required hydrocortisone replacement therapy. This case highlights an exceptionally prolonged course of cyclic ectopic ACTH syndrome characterized by extreme hormonal oscillation, reversible adrenal hyperplasia, and recurrent hypocortisolism, emphasizing the importance of long-term biochemical surveillance and individualized therapeutic adjustment.

title: When anorexia nervosa conceals Cushing syndrome: a diagnostic pitfall in hypercortisolemia.
abstract: A 37-year-old woman presented with severe hypertension, mood changes, and weight loss (body mass index 14.6 kg/m 2 ). She exhibited restrictive eating behaviors consistent with anorexia nervosa, alongside biochemical hypercortisolemia with serum cortisol 43.6 µg/dL (1204 nmol/L; reference range: 6.2-18.1 µg/dL; 170-500 nmol/L), 24-hour urinary free cortisol 430.3 µg/24 hours (1187 nmol/24 hours; reference range: <60.2 µg/24 hours; <166 nmol/24 hours), and unsuppressed adrenocorticotropic hormone of 19.1 pg/mL (4.2 pmol/L; reference range: 7.3-63.1 pg/mL; 1.6-13.9 pmol/L). The cortisol level after the 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test was 23.9 µg/dL (659 nmol/L; reference range: <1.8 µg/dL; <50 nmol/L). Cortisol remained markedly elevated after nasogastric feeding and weight restoration. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging revealed a 4 mm left anterior pituitary lesion. High-dose dexamethasone suppression, corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation, and inferior petrosal sinus sampling confirmed a pituitary source of adrenocorticotropic hormone. The patient underwent transsphenoidal resection of a corticotroph adenoma. Eleven months later, her hypertension and restrictive eating behaviors had resolved, and her mood significantly improved. Cushing syndrome can coexist with anorexia nervosa, masking typical cushingoid features and presenting with psychiatric manifestations and weight loss. Persistent hypercortisolemia despite nutritional rehabilitation should prompt dynamic endocrine testing and pituitary evaluation to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment.

title: Calcimimetic therapy modified the radiological, surgical, and histopathological features of a parathyroid adenoma.
abstract: Calcimimetics are increasingly used to control hypercalcemia before parathyroidectomy. Although treatment-induced degenerative changes have been reported in parathyroid adenomas, their effects on preoperative imaging and surgical planning remain unclear. A 70-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism was administered preoperative evocalcet (2 mg/day). After ∼2 months, serum calcium levels decreased to the hypocalcemic range, prompting drug discontinuation before surgery referral. Upon presentation, corrected serum calcium normalized to 9.1 mg/dL (SI: 2.28 mmol/L; reference range, 8.8-10.1 mg/dL [SI: 2.20-2.53 mmol/L]), whereas intact parathyroid hormone remained mildly elevated at 65.7 pg/mL (SI: 7.0 pmol/L; reference range, 10-65 pg/mL [SI: 1.1-6.9 pmol/L]). Ultrasonography revealed a right superior parathyroid lesion, with markedly decreased Doppler flow. Four-dimensional computed tomography revealed weak enhancement throughout the contrast-enhanced phase. Parathyroidectomy revealed marked fibrosis and dense adhesions around the recurrent laryngeal nerve, making dissection technically demanding, although the nerve was preserved. Histopathological examination confirmed parathyroid adenoma with extensive fibrosis, cystic degeneration, necrosis, and macrophage infiltration. Therefore, calcimimetic therapy may modify the radiological and histopathological characteristics of parathyroid adenomas and intraoperative findings relevant to surgical planning. Recognition of these treatment-induced changes may improve the interpretation of preoperative images, help surgeons anticipate dense adhesions, and facilitate meticulous surgical dissection.

title: Primary adrenal small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma in a patient with sarcoidosis and synchronous colon adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Primary adrenal neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), particularly the small cell subtype, is exceptionally rare. In patients with sarcoidosis, inflammatory lymphadenopathy may mimic a metastatic disease, making disease detection difficult. A 76-year-old man with sarcoidosis was referred for an enlarging left adrenal incidentaloma that had increased in size from 7 mm to 19 × 14 mm over 3 years. Hormonal evaluation revealed unremarkable findings; laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed because malignancy could not be excluded. Histopathological examination revealed small cell NEC with positive synaptophysin and chromogranin A staining, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 80%. One month after surgery, para-aortic lymphadenopathy was detected. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (CT) showed uptake in the para-aortic lymph nodes and ascending colon, where colonoscopy identified synchronous adenocarcinoma. The cause of the lymphadenopathy was uncertain because of coexisting sarcoidosis and colon cancer. Cisplatin plus irinotecan induced a partial response; however, disease progression was observed. CT-guided lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic NEC. Second-line amrubicin therapy reduced tumor size; comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a tumor mutation-burden-high phenotype. This case highlights diagnostic challenges in the evaluation of lymphadenopathy in patients with sarcoidosis and synchronous malignancy, emphasizing the importance of pathological confirmation for guiding appropriate management.

title: Quadriceps Strength Recovery Trajectories Associate with Pre-Operative Predictors but not Clinical Outcomes Following ACL Reconstruction.
abstract: Purpose Quadriceps weakness following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is common, however distinct longitudinal strength trajectories not have been examined. This study aimed to i) identify strength trajectories measured pre-operatively to 12 months post-ACLR, and determine associations with ii) pre-operative demographics, patient-reported outcomes (PROs: Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score [KOOS], Tegner, Marx) and ACLR concomitant surgeries, and iii) clinical outcomes post-ACLR including cartilage compositional changes (via magnetic resonance imaging [MRI] T1ρ relaxation times) and 12-month KOOS. Methods Isometric quadriceps strength was measured bilaterally pre-operatively and at 4, 6, and 12 months. Group trajectory modeling characterized longitudinal strength recovery in ACLR and uninvolved limbs, which were combined to define dual-limb recovery patterns. Tibiofemoral and patellofemoral cartilage composition was measured pre-operatively and at 12 months post-ACLR. Dirichlet regressions examined associations between trajectories and demographics, surgeries, PROs, and cartilage changes. Results 59 participants were included (58% female; age, 21.9 ± 4.7y; BMI, 24.55 ± 3.7kg/m 2). Three combined trajectories were identified: bilaterally weak (51%), which demonstrated uninvolved limb strength declines and failure to recover ACLR limb pre-operative strength; bilaterally strong (38%), which demonstrated minimal uninvolved limb declines and ACLR limb pre-operative strength recovery; and weak uninvolved, strong ACLR limb (12%). Lower pre-injury Tegner scores associated with bilaterally weak membership (p = 0.01), where probability increased from 0.27 (score of 10) to 0.61 (score of 0). Medial meniscectomy associated most with bilaterally weak membership (p<.001, 0.86 probability). No associations were found between trajectories and clinical outcomes. Conclusions While individuals who failed to restore ACLR limb strength demonstrated bilateral quadriceps weakness pre-operatively, persons who demonstrated greater pre-operative bilateral strength recovered ACLR limb strength. Medial meniscectomy associated with an inability to restore quadriceps strength.

title: Successful Kidney Transplantation Under Combined Spinal-Epidural Anesthesia in a Patient With a History of Left Pneumonectomy Due to Bronchiectasis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Kidney transplantation offers clear survival and quality-of-life advantages over dialysis, but severe pulmonary disease can complicate perioperative planning. In patients with substantially reduced respiratory reserve after pneumonectomy, general anesthesia may be considered high risk, creating uncertainty about transplant feasibility. CASE REPORT A 33-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease secondary to biopsy-proven AA amyloidosis was evaluated for preemptive living-donor kidney transplantation. He had undergone left pneumonectomy in 2015 because of bronchiectasis. Pulmonary function testing showed a mixed restrictive-obstructive pattern, with a forced vital capacity of 1.6 L (33% predicted), a forced expiratory volume in 1 second of 1.05 L (30% predicted), and a forced expiratory volume in 1 second/forced vital capacity ratio of 65%, indicating severe pulmonary impairment. Thoracic computed tomography demonstrated leftward mediastinal shift and diffuse bronchiectatic changes in the remaining right lung. Given the anticipated risk associated with general anesthesia, combined spinal-epidural anesthesia was selected. The transplant was successfully performed using a kidney from the patient's human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-identical sister. No intraoperative respiratory or hemodynamic instability occurred. Renal function rapidly improved after surgery: serum creatinine decreased from 6.6 mg/dL preoperatively to 0.63 mg/dL on postoperative day 3. Heavy proteinuria also greatly improved during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS This case demonstrates that kidney transplantation can be successfully performed under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia in carefully selected patients with severely limited pulmonary reserve after pneumonectomy. It also highlights the importance of individualized anesthetic planning and close multidisciplinary coordination for complex transplant candidates with major pulmonary comorbidities.

title: MRI-based machine learning models for differentiating Parkinson’s disease and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
abstract: Background: Parkinson’s disease (PD) and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) are neurodegenerative disorder which have Parkinsonism as core clinical feature. PD and PSP are often misdiagnosed in early phases by conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Hence the objective of the study is to evaluate accuracy of MRI based machine learning (ML) models for differentiating PD and PSP. Methods This is a retrospective study including total of 96 subjects (32 PD, 32 PSP and 32 healthy controls). The basal nuclei region such as substantia nigra (SN), caudate nucleus (CN), putamen, globus pallidus (GP), red nucleus (RN), and subthalamic nucleus (STN) were manually segmented in T2 weighted fluid attenuation inversion recovery (T2W-FLAIR) images and radiomics features (RF) were extracted. The top 20 RF were used to train and test ML models. Performance measures of ML models for differentiating PD, PSP and HC were evaluated. Results For differentiating PD from PSP, SN consistently showed highest performance achieving accuracy, F1score and AUC values of 0.95–1.00 across all the tested ML models. RN and STN also demonstrated near perfect classification with several ML models with accuracy and AUC values of 1.00. CN, putamen and GP showed moderate performance (accuracy 38% - 85%). Among classifiers, AdaBoost provided robust performance achieving AUC up to 0.89 and MCC up to 0.72 in test data sets. Conclusion MRI based radiomics models from SN, STN and RN provide the most accurate classification of PD and PSP. It can also help in diagnosis of PD and PSP which are undifferentiable in early stages of disease.

title: Vigorous physical activity and physical function are strongly associated with better health in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the impact of physical function and level of physical activity on health status and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA). Methods In total, 141 patients with long-standing r-axSpA were included in this cross-sectional cohort study. Assessments included physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI)), spinal mobility (modified Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI)), muscle function for leg strength (Timed Stands Test (TST)) and handgrip force (Grippit), amount of self-reported physical activity (vigorous physical activity, moderate physical activity, sedentary behavior), health status by ASAS Health Index (ASAS HI) and HRQoL with Short Form Survey Instrument 36-Item. Multivariable linear regression was used to analyze associations between health status, HRQoL, physical activity, muscle function, and physical function. Results The mean (SD) age was 60 (12) years, diagnosis duration was 25 (10) years, and 57% were male. Physical function and vigorous physical activity were the strongest determinants of health status and HRQoL. The models explained approximately 50% of the variation in ASAS HI and the physical aspects of HRQoL and 21% of the mental aspects of HRQoL. Participants displayed good health status (62%) by ASAS HI ≤ 5, reached the recommended level of health-enhancing physical activity (77%), had normal muscle function (TST 82% and Grippit 91%), and demonstrated physical function (55%), and spinal mobility (45%) within reference values. Conclusion This study highlights the importance of regular vigorous physical activity in older individuals living with long-standing r-axSpA since it was strongly associated with health status and HRQoL.

title: When Imaging is Negative: Endoscopic Diagnosis of a Secondary Aortoduodenal Fistula.
abstract: Aortoenteric fistula is a life-threatening aortic graft complication with a narrow opportunity for treatment. We present a patient with aortobifemoral bypass who developed recurrent anemia and melena. Despite previous upper endoscopy and colonoscopy, computed tomography angiogram, and tagged red blood cell scan, his symptoms were persistent. Capsule endoscopy showed blood in the duodenum. Push enteroscopy revealed graft erosion in the duodenum, confirming aortoduodenal fistula. He underwent aortobifemoral graft excision, and resection of the third portion of the duodenum with end-to-side duodenojejunostomy, highlighting the importance of endoscopy in timely diagnosis of aortoenteric fistulae.

title: Pulmonary CT classification based on CNN and Grad-CAM explainability using VGG16 and MobileNetV2.
abstract: Objectives This study compared the classification performance of VGG16 and MobileNetV2 models for normal-versus-lung-cancer-positive pulmonary CT image classification, with Grad-CAM used for post-hoc visual explainability. Methods A hospital-provided dataset of 550 non-contrast thoracic CT images, comprising 240 normal and 310 lung cancer-positive images, was divided into training, validation and test subsets using a patient-grouped stratified 50/10/40 split. Images were acquired at 120 kV with a 512 × 512 matrix using a NeuViz 128 CT scanner. Both models used the same preprocessing, training-only augmentation and evaluation protocol. The VGG16 model used stacked convolutional blocks, whereas MobileNetV2 used inverted residual bottlenecks with global average pooling, dropout and a sigmoid classification layer. Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, balanced accuracy, ROC-AUC, MCC and Cohen's kappa, while Grad-CAM examined decision-relevant regions. Results On the 220-image independent test set, VGG16 achieved 0.9636 accuracy, 0.9677 sensitivity, 0.9583 specificity and 0.9569 ROC-AUC. MobileNetV2 achieved 0.9909 accuracy, 0.9919 sensitivity, 0.9896 specificity and 0.9858 ROC-AUC, with fewer false-positive and false-negative predictions. Conclusions MobileNetV2 achieved stronger held-out test performance than VGG16 under identical experimental conditions. Larger multi-centre patient-level validation remains necessary before clinical deployment in CT screening workflows.

title: Equity-aware stochastic optimization of mammography screening facility location under demand and capacity uncertainty
abstract: Abstract Uneven geographic access to mammography can limit participation in breast cancer screening, particularly in rural and underserved communities. We developed a statewide planning framework that combines geospatial accessibility analysis with stochastic facility-location optimization to identify locations for new mammography facilities under uncertainty in screening demand and existing-facility capacity. The analysis included 5.58 million Texas women aged 40–74 years, 615 existing facilities, and 222 candidate locations. The model first maximized expected screening coverage and then reduced population-weighted differences in potential access across eight race and ethnicity groups without sacrificing coverage. Opening 62 facilities across 58 counties increased expected coverage from 92.47% to 98.09% and reduced expected unmet demand from 420,089 to 106,822 women annually. Between-group variance (BGV) in access decreased by 32%, while access for the worst-served group increased from 0.858 to 0.953 effective screening slots per eligible woman. All selected locations were in baseline access-gap areas; 44% were in nonmetropolitan counties and 39% established the first mammography facility in their county. Explicitly modeling uncertainty reduced expected unmet demand by 29,643 women compared with deterministic planning. These results show that a modest, equity-aware expansion of fixed mammography capacity can substantially widen screening access and narrow both racial and geographic disparities—by placing facilities where under-served populations live rather than where volume is highest—while the most remote communities are better served by mobile screening than by additional fixed sites.

title: Robot-Tracked Multi-View 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction for Quantitative Assessment of Simulated Abdominal Haemorrhage in a Tissue-Mimicking Phantom
abstract: Abstract Background Rapid identification and assessment of abdominal haemorrhage are important in trauma. Conventional 2D US is well established for detecting free abdominal fluid but is unsuited to directly quantifying irregular fluid collections. This study established a robot-tracked multi-view 3D US framework for quantitative reconstruction of abdominal free fluid in a tissue-mimicking phantom. Methods A Philips VL13-5 3D transducer on a Philips EPIQ 7 system was rigidly mounted to a Franka Emika Panda robot. US–robot hand–eye calibration used 64 manually aligned 3D US volumes and 13-fold held-out pose cross-validation. A phantom with a controllable reservoir designed to represent free-fluid accumulation within the Morison’s pouch imaging region was imaged at 70 mL, 100 mL, 120 mL, 150 mL, and 190 mL. Two sonographers acquired 122 overlapping 3D US volumes along a two-pass trajectory. Tracking-derived reconstructions were refined using semi-automatic rigid registration and expert verification. Free fluid was manually segmented in all source volumes, and reconstructed volumes were compared with target injected-volume references. Results Final calibration achieved an RMS point-to-point reconstruction error of 1.23 mm; pooled held-out RMS error was 1.27 mm. Tracking-derived reconstruction reproduced the acquisition geometry but retained residual inter-volume misalignment and underestimated free-fluid volume, with MAPE of 9.78%. Expert-verified refinement reduced MAPE to 0.90%, with absolute relative volumetric errors of 0.07–2.61%. Conclusion Tracking provided a spatial basis for multi-view 3D US reconstruction, but accurate inter-volume registration was required for reliable volumetric quantification. The framework provides a benchmark for automated registration, segmentation, and wide-field multi-aperture ultrasound development.

title: Structured Modality Dropout for Robust MRI-Based IDH Mutation Classification in Glioma
abstract: Abstract The classification of IDH gene mutation is an essential marker in the treatment of a group of brain tumors called glioma, indicating the favorability of prognosis and response to treatment. Current methods determine the IDH mutation status invasively through postoperative tissue and DNA analysis. It is favorable to predict the mutation status non-invasively from MRI scans to determine suitable surgical strategies. Existing MRI-based prediction models often assume the availability of all four MRI modalities. However, in real-world clinical settings, one or more modalities may be missing due to reasons such as image quality and inconsistent protocols. This severely impacts the performance of MRI-based deep learning models. This study proposes a structured modality dropout training strategy to improve the robustness of a 3D ResNet18 model for IDH prediction. We compared three training strategies: Baseline (no dropout), Dropout-30 (moderate), and Dropout-50 (aggressive). All three models were evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation across six realistic modality availability scenarios (all four, missing T1CE, missing FLAIR, missing T2, T1 and T2 only, T1 only). Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, and bootstrap confidence intervals (CI). Key Findings: The Baseline model performed best when all four modalities were available (AUC $0.823 \pm 0.042$), but the Dropout models showed more stable performance as the number of missing modalities increased. The Dropout-30 model showed the best calibration, with the lowest Brier score of $0.198$. Overall, Dropout-30 was the most balanced and clinically viable model, remaining the most stable across scenarios, best calibrated, and showing good generalization across scanner models.

title: Joint Classification and Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning for Cervical Cancer Detection in Histopathological Images
abstract: Abstract Correct categorization of histopathological images of the cervix is very crucial if one is to identify and treat any emerging cases of cervical cancer on time. However, this is not an easy task, given that there is so much variability within one class while there are only minute distinctions between normal and pathological tissues. In our study, we therefore develop a deep learning approach that combines contrast learning with the traditional approach of using the cross-entropy loss function to correctly categorize histopathological images of the cervix into normal or pathological tissues. Our approach is based on ResNet-50 and seeks to maximize both learning of appropriate features and correct classification of images into one of two classes: normal or pathological cervical tissues. Performance is evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation on a variety of metrics, including balanced accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, as well as average precision. For the histopathological dataset, CAISHI, this approach in all cases produces very high balanced accuracy of 96.90 ± 0.23 on average. High precision, recall, and F1 values indicate a high accuracy of abnormal region detection. In comparison to existing machine learning techniques, CNN models, transformer networks, and a few-shot learning strategy, the proposed approach demonstrates improved robustness and generalization capabilities. From the results, it can be inferred that the integration of supervised contrastive learning with deep convolutional feature extraction leads to a dramatic improvement in the representation ability and classification accuracy in the field of cervical histopathology images. The proposed framework can indeed be used as a robust interpretation solution with high potential for medical support in cervical cancer diagnosis.

title: Added Prognostic Value of MRI to CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy in the Extended Time Window.
abstract: Background In the 6-24-hour window, imaging must identify patients with salvageable tissue while avoiding delays and reperfusion of large established infarcts. The optimal imaging strategy remains controversial. Although computed tomography (CT) is widely used because of its accessibility and speed, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides more sensitive tissue characterization. This study evaluated whether adding MRI to CT was associated with clinical outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT). Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of consecutive patients with AIS due to large vessel occlusion who underwent MT between January 2022 and December 2024. Patients were grouped according to pre-procedural imaging: CT alone or MRI plus CT. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to reduce measured baseline imbalances. The primary outcomes were excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1) and 3-month mortality; symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (SICH) was the secondary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations. Results After propensity score matching, 364 patients (182 pairs) were included in the final analysis. Compared with CT alone, the MRI plus CT group demonstrated significantly lower 3-month mortality (7.1% vs 18.7%, P < 0.01) and reduced incidence of SICH (2.2% vs 7.7%, P = 0.02). No significant difference was observed in excellent functional outcome at 3 months between groups. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that MRI plus CT was independently associated with lower risks of mortality (adjusted OR=0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.72; P < 0.01) and SICH (adjusted OR=0.23, 95% CI 0.05-0.96; P =0.04). Conclusion Among patients with AIS undergoing MT within the 6-24-hour window, MRI plus CT was associated with lower 3-month mortality and SICH than CT alone, without a significant difference in excellent functional outcome. Because imaging allocation was non-randomized and quantitative infarct-core and perfusion data were unavailable, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require prospective multicenter validation.

title: Construction of a Nomogram Integrating Magnetic Resonance Imaging Features and Ephrin-A3 Expression to Predict Postoperative Overall Survival in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose Elevated EFNA3 mRNA is associated with poor prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of Ephrin-A3 immunohistochemical expression and construct a nomogram combining MRI features and Ephrin-A3 expression for postoperative OS prediction in HCC. Patients and methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 111 HCC patients, from whom MRI data were collected, and Ephrin-A3 immunohistochemistry was performed. Using an optimal cut-off value of averaged optical density (AOD) derived from Ephrin-A3 staining to predict OS, patients were categorized into high and low expression groups. The cohort was randomly split into training (70%) and validation (30%) sets. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses identified independent OS predictors, and a nomogram was constructed to predict post-surgical OS. We assessed the model's performance through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, area under the curve (AUC) measurements, Kaplan-Meier survival curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) in both datasets. Results Ephrin-A3 expression, tumor margin, nonrim arterial phase hyperenhancement, and extrahepatic metastasis were independent predictors of OS. The nomogram had concordance indexes of 0.76 and 0.72 in the training and validation sets, respectively. Time‑dependent ROC analysis showed AUCs of 0.790 and 0.776 at 36 and 60 months in the training set, and 0.737 and 0.770 in the validation set; the 12‑month AUC was not estimable due to zero events in the validation set. Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly prolonged OS in the low-risk group across both datasets. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and actual survival rates, and DCA supported the model's clinical utility. Conclusion Ephrin-A3 serves as an independent prognostic factor for OS in HCC patients after surgery, and the constructed nomogram exhibits favorable predictive performance for postoperative survival.

title: Detection of Cervical Nodal Metastasis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Using Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy: Ex Vivo Diagnostic Modeling Study.
abstract: Background Cervical nodal metastasis remains one of the strongest determinants of treatment planning and prognosis in oral squamous cell carcinoma. Histopathology remains the reference standard, but it does not provide immediate information at the point of surgical specimen assessment. Elastic scattering spectroscopy (ESS) offers rapid, label-free optical interrogation of tissue microstructure, and may support ex vivo nodal assessment. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of ESS combined with machine learning classification for ex vivo detection of cervical lymph node metastasis in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma. Methods We conducted a single-center observational ex vivo diagnostic modeling study in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma undergoing primary tumor resection and neck dissection. A total of 3 ESS spectra were acquired from each bivalved lymph node before routine histopathological processing. Internal validation used repeated nested 5-fold cross-validation grouped by patient, so every spectrum and lymph node from a patient remained in the same fold. All preprocessing, scaling, dimensionality reduction, within-model-family configuration, and hyperparameter tuning, probability calibration where required, and decision-threshold selection were restricted to training data within the nested validation process; comparisons between candidate model families were exploratory and were based on pooled patient-grouped out-of-fold predictions. Spectrum-level probabilities were aggregated within each lymph node, and histopathology was the reference standard. Results A total of 52 patients were assessed for eligibility, 45 were included, and 280 fresh lymph nodes were assessed by ESS; 96 were pathology positive, and 184 were pathology negative. Of 840 acquired spectra, 760 passed quality control. Of the 280 nodes, 274 retained at least 2 usable spectra and comprised the analytical cohort; 6 pathology-negative nodes yielded no analyzable node-level ESS result. The hybrid model was selected because it had the highest pooled patient-grouped out-of-fold node-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), with an internally validated, exploratory estimate of 0.966 (95% CI 0.929-0.988). The same out-of-fold predictions informed model-family selection and performance reporting; this estimate does not represent independent validation of a prospectively fixed final model. At the cross-validation-derived summary threshold, secondary descriptive operating characteristics were sensitivity 93.8% (95% CI 86.4%-97.6%), specificity 95.5% (95% CI 90.1%-98.3%), accuracy 94.9% (95% CI 90.4%-97.3%), positive predictive value 91.8% (95% CI 82.9%-96.3%), and negative predictive value 96.6% (95% CI 92.4%-98.8%). The Brier score was 0.063, with calibration-in-the-large of -0.03 and a calibration slope of 0.94. Patient-level sensitivity was 96% and specificity was 90%. Pathology-positive and pathology-negative nodes also showed differences across amplitude-related and shape-related spectral features. Conclusions ESS showed promising ex vivo discrimination of metastatic cervical lymph nodes in this single-center model-development and internal-validation study. The findings support further investigation of ESS as a potential pathology-triage adjunct rather than a replacement for histopathology.

title: Automated Lewis Score Estimation for Small Bowel Crohn Disease Using Capsule Endoscopy: Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Small bowel capsule endoscopy (SBCE) is widely used to evaluate small bowel involvement in Crohn disease (CD); however, manual Lewis score calculation is time-consuming and susceptible to interobserver variability. Objective This study aimed to develop and preliminarily validate a multitask deep learning system for automated Lewis score estimation in patients with small bowel CD undergoing SBCE. Methods We developed Eval-Model, a multitask framework integrating You Only Look Once (YOLO)-style lesion detection and localization for ulcers and edema, a stenosis classification branch, and a long short-term memory-based temporal regression module. The primary dataset comprised SBCE examinations from 814 patients at the Children's Hospital of Fudan University. In this dataset, 725 (89.1%) cases were included for lesion-level annotation, and 89 (10.9%) cases with expert-consensus Lewis scores were used for scoring model development and internal testing. These 89 cases comprised 49 (55.1%) training cases and 40 (44.9%) internal test cases. All splits were performed at the patient level. A retrospective same-center temporal validation cohort of 20 consecutive cases from 2026 and 5 control cases were used for preliminary assessments of temporal robustness and specificity. Results In the 40-case internal Lewis score test set, Eval-Model achieved a mean squared error of 14.693 (95% CI 8.72-22.15), root mean squared error of 3.833 (95% CI 2.95-4.71), mean absolute error of 2.9 (95% CI 2.1-3.8), R 2 of 0.82 (95% CI 0.70-0.90), and explained variance of 0.83 (95% CI 0.72-0.91). For lesion recognition, the model achieved an overall mean average precision of 0.94 with an inference time of 15 ms per frame. In the 20-case same-center temporal validation cohort, the mean squared error was 26.848 (95% CI 12.51-45.33), the root mean squared error was 5.182 (95% CI 3.54-6.73), the mean absolute error was 3.3 (95% CI 2.2-4.6), R 2 rounded to 1.00 (95% CI 0.98-1.00), and the explained variance rounded to 1.00 (95% CI 0.98-1.00). These temporal estimates require cautious interpretation because of the small, same-center cohort. Conclusions Eval-Model demonstrated preliminary feasibility for automated Lewis score estimation from SBCE in small bowel CD. The system may serve as a standardized adjunct to expert review, but larger multicenter prospective validation with independent external annotation is required before clinical deployment.

title: High-risk Human Papillomavirus Genotypes in Women Undergoing Cervical Screening in Leshan, China: Real-time and Nested Multiplex PCR.
abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the principal etiological factor in cervical precancer and cervical cancer. Regional surveillance of HR-HPV prevalence and genotype distribution is important because circulating genotypes may vary according to geography, age structure, screening access, and vaccination coverage. This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated HR-HPV infection among women undergoing routine cervical cancer screening at Leshan Maternal and Child Health Hospital, Leshan, Sichuan, China, between January 2022 and December 2024. A total of 5,000 eligible women aged 25-60 years were included. Cervical specimens were collected from the transformation zone using a sterile cytobrush and preserved in liquid-based cytology medium. Primary HR-HPV detection was performed using the Roche Cobas 4800 HPV assay, which detects HPV16 and HPV18 individually and detects 12 additional high-risk genotypes as a pooled result. Samples positive for pooled HR-HPV were further analyzed by nested multiplex PCR to identify additional genotypes. Cytology and histopathology results, where available, were reviewed and correlated with HPV detection results. Among 5,000 screened women, 612 were HR-HPV positive, corresponding to an overall prevalence of 12.2%. Single-genotype infections accounted for 65.7% of HPV-positive cases, while multiple-genotype infections accounted for 34.3%. HPV16 was the most frequent genotype, followed by HPV31, HPV56, HPV66, and HPV51. HR-HPV prevalence was highest in women aged 25-30 years and declined with increasing age. Multivariate analysis showed that age below 35 years, multiple sexual partners, smoking, and lack of prior screening were associated with higher odds of HR-HPV positivity. These findings describe the regional epidemiology of HR-HPV infection in a cervical screening cohort from Leshan and support continued genotype surveillance, while conclusions regarding genotype replacement and vaccine impact should be interpreted with caution due to incomplete vaccination history data.

title: Machine Learning, Radiomics, and Clinical Models Predicting Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis in Lung Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially fatal immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung cancer, and many machine-learning (ML), computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models have been proposed to predict it. This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and SinoMed, supplemented by citation searching and other sources, with independent dual-reviewer screening throughout and a reproducible PubMed verification search updated to August 16, 2026. Twelve peer-reviewed lung-cancer CIP-occurrence models (4,875 patients, 1,057 events) formed the main analysis; validation C-statistics were pooled on the logit scale with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp intervals, stratified by validation design. The pooled validation C-statistic was 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.75-0.88) with high heterogeneity (I 2 = 90.7%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.51-0.95, which is the decision-relevant quantity. By validation design, internal cross-validation pooled to 0.83, internal split-sample to 0.76, and only two studies reported external validation (0.84 and 0.92, described narratively). Imaging-based models (k = 8) showed numerically higher discrimination than clinical models (k = 4; 0.85 versus 0.78, moderator p = 0.46) without a statistically significant difference, and this comparison is confounded by design covariates. Estimates were stable on leave-one-out, alternative-model, cohort-overlap, and standard-error-source sensitivity analyses (range 0.80-0.84). Under the standard Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, applied independently by two reviewers with consensus resolution, two studies were at high, nine at unclear, and one at low overall risk of bias; certainty of evidence was low (very low under a stricter appraisal scenario, which left the pooled estimate essentially unchanged). Current models separate risk groups on average but remain unready for clinical use; adequately powered, externally validated, and calibration-reported models are needed.

title: Nutritional and Biochemical Correlates of Disease Severity and Hospitalization in Adults with Drug-resistant Tuberculosis: A Prospective Study from North India.
abstract: Background Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) remains a major public health challenge in high-burden countries. While microbiological diagnosis is central to management, factors determining disease severity and hospitalization at presentation are less well characterized, particularly simple clinical and biochemical markers that may aid early risk stratification. Objectives To evaluate the clinical, nutritional, radiological, and biochemical profile of adults with confirmed DR-TB and to identify factors associated with disease severity, bacillary burden, and hospitalization. Methods This prospective observational study enrolled adults (>14 years) with confirmed DR-TB treated at a tertiary care DR-TB center in New Delhi between April and December 2022. Demographic, clinical, nutritional, biochemical, radiological, and microbiological data were collected at baseline. Disease severity was assessed using chest radiograph extent and sputum smear grading. Associations were analyzed using correlation and comparative statistical methods. Results A total of 55 patients were included (mean age: 26.6 ± 13.3 years), with a female predominance (52.7%). Undernutrition was common, with a mean body mass index of 17.3 ± 2.7 kg/m2 and 63.6% of patients underweight. Greater radiographic severity correlated with lower body mass index (BMI), higher symptom burden, and higher sputum smear grades (P < 0.01). Elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels were consistently associated with cough severity, dyspnea, radiographic extent, higher smear grades, and need for hospitalization. Lower serum protein and magnesium levels were associated with higher bacillary burden. Nearly half of the patients (47.3%) required hospitalization at diagnosis, which was significantly associated with lower BMI, hypoproteinemia, and elevated ALP levels. Conclusion In adults with DR-TB, disease severity and hospitalization at presentation are closely associated with nutritional depletion and biochemical derangements in addition to microbiological burden. Simple, routinely available parameters such as BMI, serum protein, ALP, and magnesium may help identify high-risk patients early and support triage and management decisions in resource-limited settings.

title: Validation of Baveno VII Criteria using Liver and Splenic Elastography for Predicting Esophageal Varices Severity in Chronic Liver Disease: A Multiparametric, Observational Study.
abstract: Background and aims Baveno VII criteria prioritize Liver Stiffness Measurement (LSM) for portal hypertension risk stratification, primarily using transient elastography. We aimed to evaluate two-dimensional-shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) cutoffs, assess the etiology-dependent utility of spleen stiffness (SSM), and introduce a novel Combined Hepato-splenic Stiffness Index (CHSSI). Materials and methods This ambispective, observational study enrolled 100 chronic liver disease patients. Participants underwent 2D-SWE for LSM and SSM, alongside endoscopy as the reference standard. A novel multiparametric index, CHSSI, was formulated. Diagnostic accuracy for Varices Needing Treatment (VNT; Grade >= II) was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC). Results The cohort was predominantly Alcohol-related Liver Disease (ALD, 49%) and Viral Hepatitis (30%). LSM independently predicted VNT (P < 0.001), with an optimal 2D-SWE cutoff of 19.2 kPa (sensitivity 90% and specificity 82%). SSM utility diverged by etiology: it correlated significantly with variceal grade in ALD (r = 0.549, P < 0.001) but poorly in viral cirrhosis (r = 0.174, P = 0.358). The novel CHSSI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUROC 0.892) for predicting VNT. Conclusions Liver stiffness remains the most robust single-parameter surrogate for esophageal varices. However, in heterogeneous cohorts where splenic stiffness alone yields inconsistent results, novel composite indices such as CHSSI and Liver Size-stiffness Index offer superior discriminative ability. These findings support a refined noninvasive risk stratification strategy, potentially reducing unnecessary screening endoscopies.

title: Computed Tomographic Features Associated with Pulmonary Melioidosis versus Pulmonary Tuberculosis in Diabetic Patients: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
abstract: Pulmonary melioidosis is frequently mistaken for pulmonary tuberculosis because of overlapping clinical and radiological features, often delaying appropriate treatment. We conducted a retrospective comparative cohort study at a tertiary care center in southern India between January 2018 and August 2025 to compare chest computed tomography (CT) features of microbiologically confirmed melioidosis and tuberculosis in diabetic adults who underwent CT within 30 days of symptom onset. A total of 151 patients were included: 46 with melioidosis and 105 with tuberculosis. Cavitation (n = 81/105 [77.1%] versus n = 20/46 [43.5%], P <0.001) and hydropneumothorax (n = 11/105 [10.5%] versus n = 0/46 [0%], P = 0.019) were more common in tuberculosis. In contrast, when compared with tuberculosis, melioidosis was associated with more frequent bilateral lung involvement (n = 37/105 [35.2%] versus n = 26/46 [56.5%], P = 0.015), pleural effusion (n = 28/105 [26.7%] versus n = 23/46 [50.0%], P = 0.005), and hilar lymphadenopathy (n = 6/105 [5.7%] versus n = 8/46 [17.4%], P = 0.032). Despite these differences, there was substantial overlap in CT findings, with upper-lobe predominance, centrilobular nodules, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy seen in both groups. In multivariable analysis, cavitation was associated with significantly lower odds of melioidosis than tuberculosis (adjusted odds ratio: 0.25, 95% CI: 0.12-0.54, P <0.001). Pulmonary melioidosis and pulmonary tuberculosis, therefore, show substantial overlap on chest CT in diabetic patients, and imaging should be interpreted as an adjunct to targeted microbiological diagnosis rather than a substitute for it.

title: Automated Two-component Pre-CTPA ECG Risk Phenotype and 365-day Mortality among ECG-evaluated Patients with Computed Tomography-confirmed Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract: Objective Electrocardiographic abnormalities are common in acute pulmonary embolism, but their prognostic value in public waveform-linked cohorts remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated whether an interpretable automated two-component pre-CTPA ECG risk phenotype was associated with 365-day mortality among ECG-evaluated patients with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism. Method This secondary analysis used a retrospective cohort derived from MIMIC-IV-Ext-PE linked to MIMIC-IV-ECG. The source population included 1,534 unique PE-positive patients after patient-level indexing. A total of 650 patients had an ECG within 6 hours before CTPA, 571 were admission-linked, and 567 passed waveform signal-quality screening. The exposure assigned 1 point for tachycardia >100 beats/min and 1 point for V3 T-wave inversion. The primary Cox model was adjusted for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, PE subtype, ICU admission initiated at or before CTPA, and early physiologic derangement after excluding heart rate from the derangement definition. Results The primary cohort included 567 patients and 126 deaths within 365 days. Crude 365-day mortality increased across score levels: 15.0% for score 0, 26.8% for score 1, and 41.7% for score 2. In the primary model, each 1-point increase in the score was associated with higher 365-day mortality (HR 1.70 [1.36-2.13], P<0.001). The exposure-level proportional hazards diagnostic did not show clear evidence of violation (P=0.060). A stabilized inverse-probability-of-selection weighted Cox model yielded a similar estimate (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28-1.99; P<0.001), although measured selection imbalance was reduced but not eliminated. Conclusion Among ECG-evaluated patients with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism, an automated two-component pre-CTPA ECG risk phenotype was associated with higher 365-day mortality. The phenotype should be interpreted as an early prognostic marker requiring further validation rather than as a validated clinical decision tool.

title: Interstitial lung disease as the initial manifestation of systemic autoimmune disease: a narrative review of autoantibodies, biomarkers, prognosis, and management.
abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) may be the first or only clinically apparent manifestation of systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease (SARD), preceding extrapulmonary features by months or years. The European Respiratory Society/American Thoracic Society research classification of interstitial pneumonia with autoimmune features (IPAF) provides a framework for patients with interstitial pneumonia and autoimmune features who do not meet criteria for a defined SARD. Importantly, IPAF requires features from at least two of three domains - clinical, serologic, and morphologic - and cannot be assigned on autoantibody positivity alone. Extended, phenotype-directed autoantibody testing can reveal lung-dominant anti-synthetase syndrome, clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis, early systemic sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, or Sjögren's syndrome (Autoimmune epithelitis). Prognosis is heterogeneous and is driven more consistently by the fibrotic burden, usual interstitial pneumonia pattern, baseline and longitudinal pulmonary physiology, and comorbidities than by the IPAF label itself. KL-6, surfactant protein D, CCL18, MMP-7, and multiplex proteomic signatures are promising biomarkers, but none is sufficiently validated to replace serial high-resolution computed tomography and pulmonary function testing. Management should be individualised through multidisciplinary discussion. Immunomodulation is most defensible for inflammatory or SARD-like phenotypes, whereas antifibrotic therapy should be considered when progressive pulmonary fibrosis is established despite appropriate management. IPAF should therefore be viewed as a dynamic research phenotype within a continuum of lung-dominant autoimmunity, requiring longitudinal reassessment for evolution to a defined SARD.

title: Pan-cancer estimation of prognostic immune biomarkers from histopathology using artificial intelligence
abstract: Multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) assays such as ImmunoProfile provide standardized quantification of prognostic immune markers but are costly and not routinely used in clinical settings. We developed a weakly-supervised AI model, HistoProfile, to estimate intratumoral cell densities of key immune biomarkers (CD8, FOXP3, PD-1, and PD-L1) and the PD-L1 tumor proportion score from routine H&E-stained whole-slide images. Trained on a large pan-cancer cohort with paired H&E and mIF data, HistoProfile discriminated biomarker-high from biomarker-low tumors in held-out samples and tumor-specific subgroups (AUROCs of 0.78-0.89 across biomarkers). Critically, the estimated biomarkers preserved prognostic stratification in downstream survival analyses, and showed cancer-specific survival associations across TCGA cohorts where mIF is unavailable. These findings support scalable H&E-based estimation of key immune biomarker measurements for large-scale immune profiling and risk stratification.

title: RadKev: An Open-Weight Decision Model for Radiology
abstract: BackgroundMany radiology decisions, such as whether a report describes a finding or how urgently a study should be read, are choices among a fixed set of answers. Decision models return a probability for each permitted answer in one step, without generating text, and an open-weight model can run within a hospital so that patient data stay local. No decision model has yet been specialized for radiology and compared with large language models (LLMs). MethodsWe fine-tuned the general-purpose decision models Kev-27B (Qwen3.8-27B backbone) and Kev-9B on 36,109 records from public radiology datasets to obtain RadKev-27B and RadKev-9B, and compared them with the Kev models, the hosted decision models Jev and OpenAI Decisions, and the LLM Qwen3.8-27B, on 14,142 held-out questions in fifteen tasks (report reading, case diagnosis and classification, radiological knowledge). The prespecified primary outcome was task-averaged accuracy relative to Kev-27B. ResultsRadKev-27B exceeded Kev-27B by 4.9 percentage points (95% CI 3.8 to 6.2), with the largest gain in report error detection (22.6 points); RadKev-9B exceeded Kev-9B by 6.9 points (5.5 to 8.4) and did not differ detectably from Kev-27B, a model three times its size. RadKev-27B was more accurate than the hosted decision models Jev (3.0 points, 1.7 to 4.4) and OpenAI Decisions (4.8, 3.2 to 6.4), than Qwen3.8-27B without reasoning (4.7, 3.4 to 6.0) and with reasoning (2.8 points, 1.0 to 4.6) on 1,675 questions, at 132-fold lower latency (128 ms vs 16.9 s per question). At an error rate of 5%, RadKev-27B could answer 90.5% of questions and Kev-27B 76.4%. ConclusionsRadKev-27B was more accurate than two hosted decision models and an LLM of the same size, with or without reasoning, at a fraction of the latency of reasoning, and can be deployed within an institution for categorical radiology decisions after validation on local data.

title: Contrasting Patterns of Cortical Volume Change in First-Episode Schizophrenia-Spectrum Psychosis
abstract: Importance Average gray matter volume (GMV) loss in early psychosis may conceal clinically relevant differences in brain change. Objective To identify longitudinal GMV-change patterns, their cross-site correspondence, and clinical associations. Design, Setting, and Participants Prospective cohort with T1-weighted MRI acquired during 2011–2026 at 2 Czech sites; median follow-up, approximately 13 months. Participants were 222 patients with first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis and 178 healthy controls frequency-matched by site and baseline age. Exposure First-episode psychosis vs healthy control status. Main Outcomes and Measures Diagnosis-blind clustering by site of image-quality-corrected, subsequently annualized GMV change across 333 cortical parcels; longitudinal voxel-based morphometry (VBM); Global Assessment of Functioning and consensus 5-factor Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale negative-symptom scores. Results Among 400 participants (mean [SD] age, 28.2 [7.5] years), 208 (52.0%) were male. Each site independently yielded 3 clusters: C1 (near-stable GMV), C2 (pronounced decrease), and C3 (increase). Cross-site centroid correlations across 333 parcels were strong for C2 and C3 (Spearman ρ = 0.865 and 0.861); C1 correlation was weak (ρ = 0.138), as expected for near-zero profiles with little regional variation. C2/C3 correspondence supported pooling matched site-specific clusters for post hoc analyses. Pooled clusters contained 77 patients and 125 controls in C1, 66 patients and 16 controls in C2, and 79 patients and 37 controls in C3. Suffixes −P and −HC identify patient and control subgroups. To situate patient changes relative to controls, post hoc VBM revealed an unanticipated gradient of increasingly pronounced GMV reduction across C1-HC → C1-P → C2-P, prominently involving association cortex, and bilateral ventral temporal GMV increase in C3-P (familywise error–corrected P < .05). The opposite contrast along this ordering showed periventricular changes consistent with progressively greater ventricular enlargement. C2-P had the lowest mean follow-up functioning and highest mean negative-symptom severity (adjusted omnibus P = .005 and .02); clinical changes from baseline did not differ significantly among patient groups. Conclusions and Relevance Early GMV change in psychosis was not uniform but comprised two contrasting directions: a clinically relevant, control-anchored pattern of increasingly pronounced GMV loss involving default mode regions and a distinct, directionally opposing ventral temporal increase. Key Points Question What patterns of cortical gray matter volume change emerge over approximately 1 year after first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis? Findings In this 2-site cohort of 222 patients and 178 controls, nearly two-thirds of patients lay along a gradient from near-stability in controls to widespread volume decrease, whereas one-third showed an opposing ventral temporal increase. Follow-up functioning and negative symptoms differed significantly among patient groups, with the least favorable scores in those showing the greatest decrease. Meaning Directions of within-person brain change may capture clinically relevant heterogeneity obscured by average volume loss.

Cross-site centroid correlations across 333 parcels were strong for C2 and C3 (Spearman ρ = 0.865 and 0.861); C1 correlation was weak (ρ = 0.138), as expected for near-zero profiles with little regional variation. C2/C3 correspondence supported pooling matched site-specific clusters for post hoc analyses. Pooled clusters contained 77 patients and 125 controls in C1, 66 patients and 16 controls in C2, and 79 patients and 37 controls in C3. Suffixes −P and −HC identify patient and control subgroups. To situate patient changes relative to controls, post hoc VBM revealed an unanticipated gradient of increasingly pronounced GMV reduction across C1-HC → C1-P → C2-P, prominently involving association cortex, and bilateral ventral temporal GMV increase in C3-P (familywise error–corrected P < .05). The opposite contrast along this ordering showed periventricular changes consistent with progressively greater ventricular enlargement. C2-P had the lowest mean follow-up functioning and highest mean negative-symptom severity (adjusted omnibus P = .005 and .02); clinical changes from baseline did not differ significantly among patient groups.

Conclusions and Relevance

Early GMV change in psychosis was not uniform but comprised two contrasting directions: a clinically relevant, control-anchored pattern of increasingly pronounced GMV loss involving default mode regions and a distinct, directionally opposing ventral temporal increase.

Key Points

Question

What patterns of cortical gray matter volume change emerge over approximately 1 year after first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis?

Findings

In this 2-site cohort of 222 patients and 178 controls, nearly two-thirds of patients lay along a gradient from near-stability in controls to widespread volume decrease, whereas one-third showed an opposing ventral temporal increase. Follow-up functioning and negative symptoms differed significantly among patient groups, with the least favorable scores in those showing the greatest decrease.

Meaning

Directions of within-person brain change may capture clinically relevant heterogeneity obscured by average volume loss.

title: Age-, sex-, and ethnicity-stratified CMR strain reference ranges and centile-based categories from the Healthy Hearts Consortium
abstract: Background This study presents reference ranges for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain from the Healthy Hearts Consortium, while evaluating variations by demographic characteristics (age, sex, and ethnicity) and technical factors (scanner vendor, magnetic field strength). We derived reference ranges and centile-based categories for ventricular, atrial, and rapid strain parameters. The prognostic relevance of these categories was assessed by examining their associations with incident cardiovascular events. Methods The dataset included 9,088 CMR studies. Automated image analysis pipelines were established using suiteHEART (NeoSoft Inc.) and cvi42 (Circle Cardiovascular Imaging). A three-step quality control framework was applied including exclusion of incomplete data, visual assessment of image and segmentation quality, and statistical outlier removal. Ventricular strain and strain rate were measured using both software solutions. Additional cvi42-derived metrics included velocity and displacement, annular plane systolic excursion metrics, and rapid strain parameters. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges were generated using lambda–mu–sigma (LMS) modeling with penalized splines. Reference ranges were defined as values between the 2.5 th and 97.5 th percentiles. For lower-tail classification, values below the 2.5th percentile were considered mildly out-of-range and values below the 0.5th percentile at least moderately out-of-range. Differences across scanner vendors (Siemens, Philips, GE) and magnetic field strengths (1.5 T vs. 3 T) were evaluated using adjusted linear models. The prognostic relevance of selected cvi42-derived categories was evaluated in approximately 45,000 UK Biobank participants using Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Results After quality control, 8,975 CMR examinations (cvi42) and 8,992 (suiteHEART) were available for analysis; these represent software-specific analytic cohorts. Most exclusions occurred during visual quality control. Women had higher absolute ventricular and atrial strain values than men across all age groups. Left ventricular (LV) longitudinal strain and strain rate were slightly lower in older ages, whereas circumferential and radial parameters remained largely stable. Left atrial strain was also lower in older age groups, while right atrial strain did not vary by age. Annular plane systolic excursion and rapid strain metrics showed similar sex-specific patterns, with modestly lower atrial and displacement values in older groups. Ethnicity-related differences were modest, heterogeneous, and substantially smaller in magnitude than age- and sex-related differences. Technical effects were parameter specific. While LV longitudinal and circumferential strains were largely unaffected, radial strain was higher at 3 T and showed vendor-related differences. LMS-derived reference ranges and centile thresholds were applied both across all ethnicities and within ethnicity-specific analyses, and are presented stratified by age and sex. In the prognostic analysis, centile categories were most consistently associated with incident heart failure. LV longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain below the 0.5th centile were associated with significantly increased risk of incident heart failure (HRs: 9.9 to 12.4, 95% CIs 7.00–13.90 to 8.49–18.06). Conclusion This study provides age- and sex-specific reference ranges and centile-based categories for CMR-derived strain parameters in a large reference population. Age and sex represent the primary determinants of myocardial deformation, whereas scanner-related effects are parameter-specific. Values in the lower extremes of the healthy reference distribution, particularly for LV strain, are associated with increased risk of incident heart failure. These findings enable standardized, centile-based classification of myocardial strain, facilitating consistent interpretation and improving risk stratification in research and clinical practice.

title: Integration of Neuroimaging and Histopathology in a Squirrel Monkey Model of Spontaneous Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy and Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities
abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a prevalent cerebrovascular pathology in AD and contributes to amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), a major complication of current anti-amyloid immunotherapy. Despite its growing clinical importance, critical gaps remain in the development of reliable biomarkers for antemortem diagnosis of CAA. Squirrel monkeys (SQMs) are a valuable non-human primate model with translational relevance due to their universal propensity to develop abundant CAA and spontaneous ARIA in geriatric animals. The present study employed R 2 *, the apparent transverse relaxation rate, which is sensitive to susceptibility-related tissue properties, including iron content and blood oxygenation levels, to monitor age-related brain pathology in SQMs with varying CAA severity. Young, early geriatric, and late geriatric SQMs underwent 7T MRI using a dual-purpose T 2 *-w 3D multi-gradient-echo sequence for high-resolution anatomy and quantitative R 2 * mapping, alongside T 2 -w/FLAIR imaging. Whole-brain and gray matter R 2 * increased with age. In contrast, white matter R 2 * showed an initial increase followed by a late-life reversal, likely reflecting age-related changes in myelin integrity, tissue microstructure, and tissue water content. MRI-histopathology correlation linked T 2 *-w MRI hypointensities to CAA-positive iron-laden vessels associated with perivascular inflammation and, in some cases, hemosiderin deposits. Here we confirmed the occurrence of ARIA-H and ARIA-E events in geriatric animals. SQMs provided a valuable opportunity to examine the underlying pathology of spontaneous ARIA-E, revealing distinctive tissue signatures associated with its manifestation. ARIA-E hyperintensities were characterized by reactive gliosis and BBB disruption, whereas more advanced lesions exhibited perivascular lymphocytic infiltration and evidence of myelin and axonal injury. The current study presents compelling evidence linking R 2 * alterations with CAA severity and ARIA-related tissue injury, providing a foundation for further advancing early detection of CAA, ARIA risk assessment, and treatment strategies.

title: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf7 2-FTLD
abstract: C9orf72 encodes a protein that is important for both typical neurodevelopment and homeostatic processes across the lifespan. Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions constitute the most common genetic cause of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Collectively, preclinical models and clinical neuroimaging studies have observed smaller thalamic volumes in C9orf72 -associated FTLD, including in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers across 18 to 30 years old, supportive of potential neurodevelopmental origins. However, it is unknown whether asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers demonstrate volume differences in specific thalamic nuclei, as reported in older asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients; if so, normative transcriptomic patterns could reveal relevant neurodevelopmental and/or FTLD-related neurodegenerative processes. This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age. Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers ( n =72) and non-carriers ( n =48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. Smaller volumes of the pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nuclei were observed in young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers. These nuclei showed higher normative expression of transcripts involved concurrently in neurodevelopmental and C9orf72 -associated FTLD neurodegenerative processes (including lysosomal, autophagic, and small GTPase functions), and lower normative expression of CALB1 , a marker of prenatal human thalamic development. Normative expression of CALB2 (another human thalamic development marker) yielded positive correlations with C9orf72 across prenatal development to adulthood. These findings identify candidate transcripts that may provide insight into the molecular architecture leading to smaller thalamic nuclei volumes in C9orf72 -associated FTLD.
